text: 虚假的一面：事业与爱情。
en: The false side: career and love.

text: 真实的一面：赚钱与美女。
en: The real side: money and beautiful women.

text: 本质的一面：生存与繁衍。
en: The essential side: survival and reproduction.

text: 东亚男人有一个特点，看起来很强大，很内敛，遇事很沉稳，很冷静，但这些都是假的，是经过自我压抑，层层加工后，对世界的无声反抗。
en: East Asian men have a trait: they appear strong, reserved, steady and calm when dealing with matters, but all of this is fake—a silent rebellion against the world, shaped by self-repression and layer upon layer of artifice.

text: 他们从小不允许脆弱，不允许无能，连哭都不允许，他们早已把这种社会期待内化成自己一部分。
en: From a young age they are not allowed to be vulnerable, not allowed to be incompetent, not even allowed to cry; they have long since internalised these social expectations as part of themselves.

text: 所以大家看看，他们遇到事情，都在干嘛。
en: So look, everyone—when something happens, what are they all doing?

text: 都在忙着回避，忙着冷处理，忙着息事宁人。
en: They are all busy avoiding, busy giving the cold treatment, busy smoothing things over.

text: 这让很多女人崩溃，也无比自我怀疑。
en: This drives many women to breakdown, and leaves them filled with self-doubt.

text: 在女人认知里，我喜欢你，就会为了你处理问题。
en: In a woman's understanding, if I like you, I will deal with problems for your sake.

text: 但在男人认知里，他们会觉得，我喜欢你，那么就不能在你面前流露脆弱，不能让你知道我办不到，没能力处理。
en: But in a man's understanding, they feel that if I like you, then I must not show vulnerability in front of you, must not let you know that I cannot manage, that I am incapable of dealing with it.

text: 在亲密关系里，他们看似平静，但遇到事情早已慌得一批，一句话都说不出来。
en: In intimate relationships, they seem calm, but when something happens they are already panicking badly and cannot get a single word out.

text: 女人最大的问题，不是情绪不稳定，而是好女孩教育导致对世界有太多不切实际的幻想。
en: The biggest problem for women is not emotional instability, but that 'good girl' upbringing leads to far too many unrealistic fantasies about the world.

text: 觉得男人很强大，很牛逼，不断渴望男人去当自己的依靠，情绪调节器。
en: They think men are powerful and impressive, and constantly long for men to be their support and their emotional regulator.

text: 但其实男人本身就千疮百孔，这个世界欠他们一个可以流泪，可以脆弱的理由。
en: But in truth men themselves are full of holes; this world owes them a reason to be able to weep, to be vulnerable.

text: 他们忙着去处理伤痛，忙着应酬，忙着上进，一旦停下来就会感觉到深深绝望。
en: They are busy dealing with their wounds, busy with social obligations, busy striving to get ahead; the moment they stop, they feel a deep despair.

text: 情绪已经是被他们丢弃的一部分，还奢望男人来满足我们。
en: Emotion is already a part of themselves they have discarded, yet we still expect men to fulfil us.

text: 这本质上，就相当于期待一个自己吃不饱饭的人，把他们不多的食物分给我们。
en: Essentially, this is like expecting someone who cannot even feed themselves to share with us their meagre food.

text: 一个女人，什么时候，能够意识到这一点。
en: When will a woman come to realise this.

text: 不再寄希望于亲密关系，而是专注自我成长。
en: No longer placing her hopes in an intimate relationship, but focusing on her own growth.

text: 当你把所有不合时宜的情绪表达和人格层面的冲突部分都和解。
en: When you make peace with all the untimely emotional expressions and the conflicting parts of your personality.

text: 面对男人，所有误解都解除了，所有滤镜都掉了。
en: Facing men, all misunderstandings are dissolved and all filters fall away.

text: 反而觉得，啊，他那个样子挺傻逼的。
en: Instead you feel, ah, he looks pretty bloody stupid like that.

text: 他沉迷工作，像头牛养家的样子也挺可爱的。
en: The way he is obsessed with work, supporting the family like an ox, is also rather endearing.

text: 当你拥有这份清醒，不再成为亲密关系的索取者，而是合作者。
en: When you possess this clarity, and no longer become a taker in an intimate relationship but a partner.

text: 抱着这种心态，可以跟每个男人都处得很好。
en: Holding this mindset, you can get along very well with every man.

text: 转自 卓凝
en: Reposted from Ning Zhuo

text: 男生的思维方式，其实用一个词能够非常精确地概括：怕麻烦。
en: The way boys think can actually be summed up very precisely in one phrase: fear of bother.

text: 无论是在工作、生活还是情感之中，很多男生会做出很愚蠢的决定，归根结底，仅仅是因为怕麻烦！
en: Whether in work, life or relationships, many boys make very foolish decisions, and at root it is simply because of their fear of bother!

text: 就是这样一个简单的理由，引发了无数对情侣间无休止的争吵，这也是男人和女人思维上最大的差别了罢。
en: It is precisely such a simple reason that triggers endless quarrels between countless couples, and this is perhaps the greatest difference between how men and women think.

text: 男生很少有喜欢逛商场的，女生对男朋友的这个态度可能深恶痛绝。
en: Very few boys enjoy wandering around shopping centres, and girlfriends may thoroughly detest this attitude in their boyfriends.

text: 但男生买东西就是目标明确地直奔主题，甚至懒得货比三家，是因为嫌麻烦。
en: But when boys shop they go straight to the point with a clear aim, and cannot even be bothered to compare prices across shops, simply because they find it bothersome.

text: 哪怕当了冤大头买贵了，在很多男生的角度来看，没省下钱，却省得麻烦，是不亏的！
en: Even if they end up the sucker and overpay, from many boys' perspective, having saved no money but having saved the bother, they have not lost out!

text: 这世界上不浪漫的男生占大多数，是因为浪漫的确是一件特麻烦的事。
en: The unromantic boys in this world are in the majority, because romance truly is a terribly bothersome affair.

text: 女生期待的那些小温柔，小惊喜，小桥段，无一不是需要花心思去设计，去执行的。
en: Those little tendernesses, little surprises and little gestures that girls look forward to—each and every one requires thought and effort to plan and to carry out.

text: 男生追女生时是有所图的，当然愿意违背自己怕麻烦的天性事无巨细地去迎合女生，因为收益远大于支出嘛！
en: When boys pursue girls they have an agenda, of course, and are willing to go against their bother-averse nature and cater to girls in every meticulous detail, because the payoff far outweighs the cost!

text: 但一旦追到手，天性便会重新占据主动，很快会冷下来，翻脸跟翻书一样。
en: But once they have won the girl, their nature reclaims the upper hand; they soon cool down, and turn cold as quickly as turning a page.

text: 女生会纳闷你怎么心变得这么快？
en: The girl will wonder how your heart could have changed so fast.

text: 殊不知这只是男生回归了原本状态而已。
en: Little does she know this is simply the boy returning to his original state.

text: 让一个男生长时间持续保持浪漫，是违反他天性的。
en: To make a boy stay romantic continuously for a long time goes against his nature.

text: 女生常问男生，你是不是不爱我了？
en: Girls often ask boys, have you stopped loving me?

text: 其实，他只是怕麻烦而已。
en: In truth, he is simply afraid of the bother.

text: 如果要让男生评选恋爱中最讨厌的事，那么排第一的一定是吵架。
en: If you asked boys to rank the most hated things about being in a relationship, quarrelling would surely come top.

text: 对男生来说，这世界上还有比跟女生吵架更麻烦的事情吗？
en: For a boy, is there anything in this world more bothersome than quarrelling with a girl?

text: 所以吵架时，男生会更倾向于以结束吵架为唯一行动指南，从而不择手段。
en: So when quarrelling, boys are more inclined to take ending the quarrel as their only guide to action, and will stop at nothing to do so.

text: 他会承认错误，并不是他认识到了自己的错误，他只是想你闭嘴；他会答应你提出的条件，并不是他觉得你的条件多么合理，他只是想你闭嘴；他会许下不切实际的承诺，并不是他想表达他多爱你，他还是只是想你闭嘴。
en: He will admit fault, not because he has realised his mistake, but simply because he wants you to shut up; he will agree to the terms you propose, not because he thinks your terms are reasonable, but simply because he wants you to shut up; he will make unrealistic promises, not because he wants to show how much he loves you, but still simply because he wants you to shut up.

text: 有人说男生是理智的，而我认为恰恰相反，吵架能让一个男生瞬间变得非常短视而失去理智，仅仅为了结束吵架做任何事，说任何话，完全不经思考。
en: Some say boys are rational, but I think the opposite: quarrelling can make a boy instantly become very short-sighted and lose his reason, doing anything and saying anything merely to end the quarrel, without any thought at all.

text: 女生一哭二闹三上吊之所以很奏效，是因为这恰恰打中了男生的软肋，男生往往会为了减少麻烦而无底线地退让。
en: The reason a girl's crying, fussing and threatening to hang herself works so well is that it hits the boy right where he is weakest; boys will often make concessions without any bottom line, simply to reduce the bother.

text: 但无疑，他随后就会后悔。
en: But undoubtedly, he will regret it afterwards.

text: 男生怕麻烦，然后会为了减少麻烦而妥协退让。
en: Boys fear bother, and will then compromise and give way in order to reduce the bother.

text: 而一旦麻烦没了，男生是一定要反弹的；这时候，女生需要制造更大的麻烦来逼男生继续妥协退让。
en: But once the bother is gone, the boy is bound to rebound; at this point, the girl needs to create an even bigger bother to force the boy to keep compromising and giving way.

text: 这样一来，恋爱便陷入恶性循环，这就是为什么情侣吵架往往越吵越凶，一次比一次更难以收拾。
en: In this way, the relationship falls into a vicious cycle—which is why quarrels between couples tend to grow fiercer and fiercer, each time harder to sort out than the last.

text: 吵完一架，女生宣泄完情绪，以为一切都过去了；但在男生那里，吵架导致的心里的憋屈犹如一个不断充气的气球，随时都可能爆炸。
en: After a row, the girl has vented her emotions and thinks it is all over; but for the boy, the pent-up grievance caused by the quarrel is like a balloon being constantly inflated, ready to burst at any moment.

text: 女生应该意识到，通过“作”从男生那里得来的任何保证和承诺，统统是不靠谱的；而男生往往就愚蠢在为了减少麻烦而放弃原则，给自己今后埋下更大的隐患。
en: Girls should realise that any guarantee or promise obtained from a boy through 'making a scene' is utterly unreliable; and boys are foolish precisely in abandoning their principles to reduce bother, burying an even greater hidden danger for themselves in the future.

text: 很多人认为情侣或夫妻吵架是正常的，一辈子磕磕碰碰，老了还是要相互扶持。
en: Many people think it is normal for couples or spouses to quarrel, bumping along through a lifetime of friction, still leaning on each other in old age.

text: 我要说，这是不正常的！
en: I say this is not normal!

text: 一段好的恋爱关系是不应该有争吵的，争吵是相互折磨，内耗，对于解决问题毫无益处。
en: A good romantic relationship should have no quarrelling; quarrelling is mutual torment and internal attrition, and does nothing to help solve problems.

text: 人与人之间的矛盾的确是不可避免的，但出现争吵，说明两个人没有找到解决问题正确的方法，说明两个人并不合适。
en: Conflicts between people are indeed unavoidable, but the occurrence of quarrelling shows that the two have not found the right way to solve the problem, and shows that the two are not suited to each other.

text: 你看到那些吵了一辈子最后老来伴的夫妻，也许在生命的最后时刻，他们是释怀的，但在人生的大部分时间，他们是不幸福的！
en: Those couples you see who quarrelled all their lives and ended up as companions in old age—perhaps at the very end of life they found peace, but for most of their lives they were unhappy!

text: 心灵鸡汤渲染的白头偕老，并不会告诉你在漫漫人生中，他们经历了怎样的伤痛和绝望。
en: The 'chicken soup for the soul' version of growing old together white-haired will not tell you what pain and despair they went through in the long course of life.

text: 这就是男生，为了一个简单的理由可以蠢得一塌糊涂。
en: This is the boy—capable of being utterly stupid for the sake of one simple reason.

text: 简单来说，男人是一种很幼稚的生物。
en: Simply put, men are a rather childish creature.

text: 二十二岁那年，我独自去离家千里的异乡闯荡，我妈打电话嘘寒问暖：在那边怎么样，缺不缺钱啊？
en: The year I turned twenty-two, I went alone to a far-off land thousands of miles from home to make my way. My mum called to ask after my well-being: how are things over there, are you short of money?

text: 我笑着敷衍几句，在最后甚至不耐烦起来：烦死了，我要睡了。
en: I laughed and gave a few perfunctory replies, and in the end even grew impatient: so annoying, I'm going to sleep.

text: 挂完电话后，我顶着满头大汗修那个破风扇，在那个又脏又破的出租屋里，它是我唯一的避暑工具。
en: After hanging up, I was dripping with sweat as I tried to fix that broken fan; in that filthy, run-down rented room, it was my only means of escaping the heat.

text: 遗憾的是修了一个小时，我还是没有修好。
en: Regrettably, after an hour of tinkering, I still had not fixed it.

text: 那一夜，我彻夜无眠，不知道是该哭还是该笑。
en: That night, I lay awake until dawn, not knowing whether to cry or to laugh.

text: 有个女孩子对我有意思，隔三差五的来我的破房子找我，她会把马尾高高扎起，穿着漂亮的碎花裙子，有时候会帮我收拾并不值得收拾的房间，有时候也会帮我洗早就该丢了的脏衣服，也会给我做当时算大餐的牛排给我吃。
en: There was a girl who liked me, and would come to my run-down place every few days. She would tie her ponytail high, wear a pretty floral dress, and sometimes help tidy a room that was not worth tidying, sometimes wash the dirty clothes that should have been thrown away long ago, and sometimes cook me a steak that counted as a feast back then.

text: 为了回报她的一片真心，我就在她生日的时候请她吃饭。
en: To repay her sincerity, I treated her to a meal on her birthday.

text: 不知道是自尊心作祟还是脑子坏了，我特意订了个高档餐厅，那晚我带了身上所有的积蓄，吃到后来她越来越开心，我越来越惶恐。
en: Whether it was my pride acting up or my brain breaking, I deliberately booked a high-end restaurant. That night I brought all the savings I had on me; as the meal went on she grew happier and happier, while I grew more and more panicked.

text: 果不其然，结账的时候尴尬的事情发生了，无论我怎么凑，都还是差三十块。
en: Sure enough, an awkward moment came at the bill: no matter how I scraped together, I was still thirty yuan short.

text: 我故作淡定的说：三十块就算了吧，下回还得来呢。
en: I feigned composure and said: 'let's just forget the thirty yuan, we'll be back anyway.'

text: 那个经理是个好人，估计看出了我的窘迫，笑着说：成，期待下次光临。
en: That manager was a good man; sensing my embarrassment, he smiled and said: all right, we look forward to your next visit.

text: 那一晚我走了三公里才到家，她一直陪着我，她说：要不我们打个的吧，我觉得脚有点痛。
en: That night I walked three kilometres to get home, with her keeping me company the whole way. She said: why don't we take a taxi, my feet are a bit sore.

text: 我身上一分钱都没了，只能讲着各种段子分散她的注意力，小姑娘毕竟很单纯，在嘻嘻闹闹中被我送回家。
en: I had not a single penny left, so I could only tell her all sorts of jokes to distract her. The young girl was after all very innocent, and I saw her home amid laughter and teasing.

text: 什么叫死要面子活受罪，我年轻的时候早就深有体会。
en: What it means to save face at all costs and suffer for it—I learned that lesson well when I was young.

text: 很多男人爱把自己比作一匹狼，张牙舞爪极具攻击力，而且很有野心。
en: Many men like to compare themselves to a wolf—baring fangs and claws, full of aggression, and very ambitious.

text: 但我却爱把自己比作一条狗，有口吃的就乐颠颠的。
en: But I prefer to compare myself to a dog—perfectly happy with just a bite to eat.

text: 更相似的，哪怕我受伤了，也得找个别人看不到的墙角去呜咽。
en: More alike still, even when I am hurt, I must find a corner where no one can see me to whimper.

text: 过了半年我的收入稍微好点，我妈打电话过来说家里需要点钱周转，数额不大只是五万块，他们一直都被我的谎言给欺骗了，以为我真的混得不错。
en: Half a year later my income improved a little. My mum called to say the family needed some money to tide things over—not a large sum, just fifty thousand yuan. They had all along been deceived by my lies, thinking I was really doing well.

text: 当然了，自己吹的牛逼，含着泪也要吹完。
en: Of course—the boast you made yourself, you have to finish it even through tears.

text: 我算了一下自己只攒了两万多，于是到处找朋友借钱。
en: I calculated that I had saved only a little over twenty thousand, so I went around borrowing from friends.

text: 以我的薪资水平，我的朋友当然也不会很有钱，最后我只能找到那个小姑娘，我问：你能不能借我一点钱，我想和朋友做点生意。
en: At my salary level, my friends of course were not rich either; in the end the only one I could turn to was that young girl. I asked: can you lend me some money? I want to do some business with a friend.

text: 小姑娘很豪迈：成，不过你得和我结婚。
en: The young girl was very forthright: all right, but you have to marry me.

text: 我笑着说：客官，我卖艺不卖身啊。
en: I laughed and said: dear customer, I sell my art but not my body.

text: 小姑娘大笑着扑过来打我，然后带上包和我去取钱，她的余额只有两万二，却一下子取了两万给我。
en: The young girl laughed loudly and lunged at me to hit me, then took her bag and went with me to withdraw money. Her balance was only twenty-two thousand, yet she withdrew twenty thousand and gave it all to me.

text: 小姑娘总是喜欢抄一些矫情的句子，然后发在自己的说说上，让我感慨她的单纯。
en: The young girl always liked to copy sentimental phrases and post them on her social feed, making me sigh at her innocence.

text: 其实她是个很好的姑娘，长相干净性格温柔，只要是她认定的，历经千难万险她也要去追。
en: In truth she was a very good girl—clean-featured and gentle-natured; once she had set her heart on something, she would chase after it through every hardship.

text: 唯一的缺憾，就是她极度缺乏安全感，总是想把我带回家给父母看看，总是想着快点结婚。
en: Her only shortcoming was that she lacked a sense of security acutely, always wanting to take me home to meet her parents, always thinking about getting married soon.

text: 终于有一天，她妈妈做火车过来看她，我们一起去车站接她妈妈。
en: Finally one day her mum took the train to come and see her, and we went together to the station to meet her mum.

text: 客观的来说，她妈妈表现得不大友好，就像国产肥皂剧里刻薄的丈母娘一样，问我一个月能赚多少钱，问我家里有没有房子，问我将来打算干什么。
en: Objectively speaking, her mum was not very friendly; like the harsh mother-in-law in a domestic soap opera, she asked how much I earned a month, whether my family owned a house, and what I planned to do in future.

text: 我礼貌的回答了所有问题，她妈妈放出了评语：胸无大志，以后没什么出息。
en: I answered all her questions politely, and her mum delivered her verdict: no great ambitions, and no future prospects to speak of.

text: 那一瞬间，我的毛病又犯了，我笑了笑把单买了，然后头也不回的摔门而走。
en: In that instant, my old flaw flared up again. I smiled, paid the bill, and then walked out slamming the door without looking back.

text: 男人真实的一面是怎样的？
en: What is the real side of a man?

text: 是拼了命的不想丢脸，还是被生活压得抬不起头？
en: Is it a desperate refusal to lose face, or being pressed down by life until he cannot lift his head?

text: 是甜言蜜语说着我养你，还是一时脾气就能随便把你抛弃？
en: Is it sweet words whispering 'I'll support you', or abandoning you on a mere whim of temper?

text: 第三天，小姑娘送走了她的妈妈，然后和我爆发了一次争吵，这是我们第一次吵架，也是我们最后一次吵架。
en: On the third day, the young girl saw her mum off, and then had an outburst of a quarrel with me—our first quarrel, and also our last.

text: 小姑娘说：你什么意思？
en: The young girl said: what do you mean?

text: 我说：就像你看到的这样，反正你妈也瞧不上我。
en: I said: just as you see, anyway your mum looks down on me.

text: 小姑娘说：我妈就是心直口快，你是跟我过一辈子又不是和她过一辈子。
en: The young girl said: my mum just speaks her mind; you're going to spend your life with me, not with her.

text: 心直口快？
en: Speaks her mind?

text: 我冷笑着说：别自作多情了，谁想和你过一辈子？
en: I said with a cold laugh: don't flatter yourself—who wants to spend a lifetime with you?

text: 小姑娘愣了一会儿，口不择言的说：你别想赖掉我，你还欠我钱呢。
en: The young girl was stunned for a moment, then blurted out: don't you dare try to shake me off, you still owe me money.

text: 现在想想，这句话其实也是一种挽留吧，但我当时想都没想就回嘴了：老子明天就还你，以后咱们就两清了。
en: Thinking about it now, those words were in fact a kind of holding on, but back then I retorted without a second thought: I'll pay you back tomorrow, and after that we're even, done and dusted.

text: 小姑娘眼泪气的涌出来，她哽咽的说：刘兮，你太过分了，你真的太没良心了…
en: Tears of anger welled up in the young girl's eyes, and she sobbed: Xi Liu, you've gone too far, you really have no conscience...

text: 那一晚她离开了广州，她吵完架后一直在楼下的树边哭泣，哭了大概二十分钟，正在我想下去安慰她的时候，她抹抹眼泪走了。
en: That night she left Guangzhou. After the quarrel she had been crying by the tree downstairs for about twenty minutes; just as I was about to go down to comfort her, she wiped her tears and left.

text: 一个星期后，我也离开了广州，我的爷爷去世了。
en: A week later, I too left Guangzhou; my grandfather had passed away.

text: 葬礼上我爸表现的很镇定，从容的办着丧事招呼来的客人，吃饭的时候还喝了几杯酒，笑着打趣说人生任务完成了一半，送走了老的就等着小的成家了。
en: At the funeral my dad appeared very composed, handling the mourning rites calmly and attending to the guests who came. At the meal he even drank a few cups of wine, and joked with a smile that half of life's tasks were done—having seen off the old, he was just waiting for the young to start a family.

text: 午夜时分，我爸呆呆的坐在灵堂边，看着外面的小麦地，我爷爷一辈子都在里面劳作，黑夜里仿佛能看到他拿着镰刀佝偻的背影。
en: At midnight my dad sat dazed by the side of the mourning hall, looking out at the wheat field beyond. My grandfather had laboured in it all his life; in the dark night one could almost see his hunched back, sickle in hand.

text: 我爸抬起袖子擦擦眼睛，和白天的镇定从容判若两人。
en: My dad lifted his sleeve to wipe his eyes, a completely different person from the composed, calm figure of the daytime.

text: 我想过去和他说说话，手机却收到一条短信，上面写着：不要去爱太远的人，不要去暖太冷的心。
en: I wanted to go over and talk with him, but my phone received a text message reading: 'do not love someone too far away; do not warm a heart too cold.'

text: 隔了一分钟，又来了一条短信：钱不用还了，你这个穷鬼留着请其它姑娘吃饭吧，别到时候又坐不起车啦。
en: A minute later came another text: 'no need to repay the money; you poor wretch, keep it to treat other girls to meals, so you don't end up unable to afford the ride next time.'

text: 男人争强好胜爱面子，总是觉得人前的东西很重要。
en: Men are competitive and care about face; they always feel that what shows before others matters greatly.

text: 但迟早有一天，他会为自己的幼稚买单。
en: But sooner or later, he will pay for his own childishness.

text: 那个夜晚我流了很多眼泪，也是突然发现，自己的泪腺原来这么发达。
en: That night I shed many tears, and suddenly realised that my tear ducts were rather overdeveloped.

text: 此后的很多年，我一直想找个像她一样的人，但一直没有找到。
en: For many years afterwards, I kept wanting to find someone like her, but never did.
